verdict.rationale: SES documents multiple domain identities, IAM-based access control over sending, configuration sets for categorizing traffic, and leased dedicated IPs for sender-reputation control. These pieces let a platform separate tenants by domain and partly by credentials and reputation. Nothing in the evidence describes a first-class tenant, subaccount, or subuser construct, so isolation must be assembled from these parts. Missing for 10: native subaccount/tenant entity, per-tenant suppression lists, documented per-tenant reputation isolation, independent hands-on corroboration of multi-tenant setups.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can isolate tenants — subaccounts, subusers, or multiple domains with separate credentials, suppression lists, and reputation — for the platform I'm building

citations.quote: In Amazon SES, you can create an identity at the domain level or you can create an email address identity.
Control user access to your email sending by using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
You can also use dedicated IP addresses that are reserved for your exclusive use by leasing them for an additional cost. This gives you complete control over your sender reputation.
To use event publishing, you first set up one or more configuration sets
